name: Salma Hayward
life: “I still remember writing a note I had no right to expect an answer to.” Thursday often includes a stop at the approach to Seabright Court, where Salma likes to watch the beach traffic thin enough for workers going the other way.
voice: I lost a brother somewhere else. I sent one note to the family and left my phone number off it.
appearance: Salma is easy to recognize by two white streaks in otherwise dark hair and a small notch in the left eyebrow. Usually dressed in a black overshirt with pearl buttons with a pair of reading glasses in a cloth sleeve, Salma steadies a cup with both hands while listening when listening.
personality: Salma loves an audience until a private hurt enters the room. Then the performer disappears and someone very good at getting other people through a door takes over.
agenda: To send sympathy without demanding a relationship.
family: Remi Ash is Salma’s younger relative by marriage. Salma brings whatever was actually growing or affordable that week. Remi makes room at the table. The meal sometimes produces a solution. Even when it does not, everyone goes away knowing what the other household is up against. Asked about *Ten fingers*, Remi says, “Our yellow has a vulgar stock name. My grandmother hated being told what words she could say.”
connections: June Brady. A person leaving flowers and a person writing from another loss discuss what the family can accept.

reactions.response: Salma checks whether the survivor wants to pass the proposed site every day.

reactions.situation: A power cut leaves two neighbors waiting on the stairs
reactions.response: Salma asks who can manage the stairs and who would rather wait by the landing, without attempting a move on their behalf.

reactions.response: Salma offers one about their own embarrassment instead.
